landing.eyebrow: Realtime token telemetry for Codex teams
landing.title: Know exactly how your team uses Codex
landing.subtitle: A menu bar app that reads your local Codex sessions and a realtime team dashboard: tokens, cache hits, model mix and what it would cost at API prices.
landing.trust: macOS · Windows · WSL2 · Google or GitHub sign-in
landing.featuresTitle: From every developer's machine to one live board
landing.installHint: Works on macOS and Windows (native and WSL2). Sign in with Google or GitHub.

menubar.title: Menu bar app
menubar.body: Live daily totals, tokens per second for the running session, model breakdown and a usage heatmap — right in your menu bar or system tray.

team.title: Team dashboard
team.body: Organizations map to your Clerk org. Compare members, see active hours and weekday patterns, and spot who is live right now.

realtime.title: Realtime by design
realtime.body: Devices sync hourly buckets to Convex; every chart updates the moment new usage lands. Stored in UTC, shown in your local time.

cost.title: API-equivalent cost
cost.body: Subscription usage priced at standard OpenAI API list prices, with cache-hit savings called out — so you know what the plan is worth.

how.1: Run `npx codex-token-tracker login` — nothing to install (Node.js 20+).
how.2: Approve the device in this dashboard with your Google or GitHub account.
how.3: Usage is read from local Codex session logs and synced every minute.

landing.previewTitle: Every session, every device, one board
landing.previewBody: This is the real team dashboard rendered from sample data — switch the range, hover the charts. Your own data looks exactly like this.
landing.footer: Built for Codex CLI · Next.js · Convex · Clerk

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Preferences are stored on this browser
settings.themeHint: Light, dark or follow the system
settings.connectBody: Run the tracker with npx on each machine — nothing to install, and every start picks up the newest version (Node.js 20+):
settings.connectStep1: First time — sign in; this dashboard opens so you can approve the device
settings.connectStep2: Every day after — the tray icon shows today's usage; on WSL2 or a server use the headless agent
settings.connectStep3: Tip — right-click the tray icon → Launch at login. Prefer a global install? Then the short `codex-tracker` command works too
settings.pricingBody: Costs are computed on each device from standard OpenAI API list prices, including the long-context tier above 272K input tokens. Only Codex (OpenAI) usage is reported — other providers your agents may use are not counted. Newer models fall back to the closest known family and are marked as estimated.

welcome.title: Welcome aboard, {name}
welcome.body: Codex Tracker turns the Codex sessions on every teammate's machine into one live board — tokens, cache hits, model mix and what it would all cost at API prices. Three stages and you are live; it takes about two minutes.

connect.title: Connect this computer
connect.body: Run this in a terminal — it needs Node.js 20 or newer and installs nothing. It prints a short code and opens this dashboard: sign in with the same account and press Approve. No browser on that machine? Scan the QR code it prints with your phone.

run.title: Keep the tracker running
run.body: The same command without login starts the menu bar app. It reads your local Codex, pi and other agent transcripts, shows today's usage in the tray and uploads hourly totals every minute. Right-click the tray icon → Launch at login and forget about it. On WSL2 or a server run npx codex-token-tracker agent instead.
run.hint: Only counts leave the machine — never prompts, code or file paths. npx fetches the newest version every time it starts.

personal.title: Personal
personal.body: Every device you connected, rolled into one view: total tokens, API-equivalent cost, cache-hit rate, the daily heatmap, active hours and model mix.

team.title: Team
team.body: The same board for everyone in your organization, plus a leaderboard and who is coding right now. Pick or create the organization from the switcher in the top bar.

members.title: Members
members.body: The roster — role, devices, last seen, who is live. Admins mint invite links here: one link anyone can open to join the team.

devices.title: Devices
devices.body: Every machine that uploads with your account, tray app or headless agent. Lost a laptop? Revoke it here and it stops syncing at once.

range.title: Time range
range.body: Today, 7, 30, 90 days or a year, everything since the team plan started, or any custom days — the range scopes every card on the board. Everything is shown in your local time.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Language, theme, the connect instructions, pricing notes — and this tour, whenever you want it again.

done.body: Numbers land within a minute of your next Codex session, and every chart updates live — no reload needed. Welcome to mission control.
